summary: You can upgrade to 2.6 from the latest 2.4 or 2.5. From 2.5 there are no infrastructure changes since platform gateway already exists, but authentication methods and users migrated from 2.4 must be finished first: unmigrated users are removed, and 2.4 controller users who never logged into 2.5 cannot log in through the gateway, keeping only direct Automation Execution access.
questions: Can I upgrade directly from AAP 2.4 to 2.6?
What must I do before upgrading from 2.5 to 2.6?
What happens to users who never logged into AAP 2.5?
Do I need to migrate authenticators before upgrading to 2.6?

answer_card.title: Before upgrading to AAP 2.6
answer_card.answer_md:
- Be on the **latest 2.4 or 2.5** release first.
- From 2.5: no infrastructure or architecture changes; the platform gateway already exists.
- If you came from 2.4 to 2.5, **finish migrating authentication methods and users** before 2.6, because the legacy authenticators are removed.
- Users not fully migrated are **removed** in 2.6.
- 2.4 controller users who never logged into 2.5 cannot log in through the gateway. Have everyone log in to 2.5 before upgrading.
